newsitem.title: FINLAND: Enso says Sep-Dec profit exceeded May-Aug.
newsitem.headline: Enso says Sep-Dec profit exceeded May-Aug.

text.p: Finnish forest industry group Enso Oy said in a statement on Wednesday that its profit in the final tertial (September-December) of 1996 had exceeded the profit of the second tertial (May-August).
"The financial result for the last four months of 1996 met expectations. Despite the difficult market situation the result was profitable and better than in the previous four months," Enso said.
In May-August 1996, Enso's operating profit was 663 million markka, according to the company's January-August interim report. Group May-August net sales were 8.37 billion markka.
Enso's January-August operating profit was 1.90 billion markka, down from 3.56 billion in the first eight months of 1995.

Referring in Wednesday's statement -- released with the announcement of the launch of a 1.0 billion markka seven-year serial bond -- to the final tertial of 1996, Enso said: "The market situation in most product groups improved slightly with the exception of the publication papers division."
Demand for newsprint and magazine papers had weakened and prices fallen, Enso said, adding production of these grades had had to be restricted due to the fall in demand. It did not elaborate.
Looking ahead, Enso said Norscan pulp inventories should fall substantially before it would be possible to raise pulp or fine paper prices.
"Should the high level of Norscan pulp inventories remain unchanged from the end of December the price increases will probably have to be postponed until spring," Enso said.
"A substantial decrease in the level of pulp inventories would be required to implement the price increase of pulp and fine papers," it said.
